statement.title: Globally benchmarked methods for informed decisions about health and welfare.
paragraphs: We conduct rigorous outcome and impact evaluations, using quasi-experimental and counterfactual methods to measure effectiveness and causal attribution, and mixed-method frameworks that integrate qualitative insight with quantitative techniques.
Our gender-transformative evaluation approaches identify structural barriers and lead to equity-driven program improvements, so that coverage reaches the people a program was designed for.

scene.eyebrow: Who is reached, and what changed
scene.title: Every dot is a person. Evidence decides what happens next.
scene.lead: Five moves of monitoring, evaluation, research, learning and adaptation (MERLA), drawn on one population.

steps.label: Measure
steps.title: Monitoring and results measurement
steps.text: We design and deploy secure, scalable data systems — context-specific, high-integrity data ecosystems that strengthen decisions, transparency and accountability.
points: Real-time monitoring with interactive dashboards and geospatial tools
Capacity building for national governments, donors and development organizations in high-quality monitoring frameworks

steps.label: Compare
steps.title: Impact evaluation with a counterfactual
steps.text: Outcome and impact evaluations using quasi-experimental and counterfactual methods, with data collection benchmarked to World Bank and OECD-DAC criteria, randomized methods and DFID practice.
points: Mixed-method frameworks for a holistic assessment

steps.label: Include
steps.title: Gender-transformative evaluation
steps.text: We look for the structural barriers that keep some people out, so that program improvements are driven by equity.

steps.label: Adapt
steps.title: Fit-for-purpose and operational research
steps.text: Evaluation designed for the sector and adapted to local priorities — including climate resilience, global health (for example, neglected tropical disease programming), education and sustainable development — with real-time operational research to find bottlenecks and improve resource efficiency.
points: “Pause and Reflect” workshops and continuous learning cycles
Most Significant Change and participatory research alongside econometric analysis

steps.label: Cost
steps.title: Comparing the options under time pressure
steps.text: For decision-makers who need evidence quickly, we systematically compare policy alternatives, run economic, financial and environmental cost-benefit analyses and project the impact of each option.
